answer: Cross-epoch behavioural consistency rule: each identity’s action profile is hashed per epoch into a fixed-size summary, and a sybil must keep every clone on the same behavioural prism across epochs or the divergence flags the cluster. An island of clones that drifts in timing, counterparties, or task mix breaks consistency and gets filtered. Enforcing this forces the attacker to synchronize and maintain plausible history for each raven identity, paying continuous compute and coordination cost per clone rather than a one-time fee.
